title: How to change the document language in Google Docs on Mac: browser steps and fixes
metaTitle: How to Change Document Language in Google Docs on Mac
description: How to change the document language in Google Docs on Mac: use File > Language for this file, Translate document for a copy, and fix common errors.
targetKeyword: how to change the document language in google docs on mac
secondaryKeywords: change language in google docs browser
intro: To change the document language in Google Docs on Mac, open the file, then go to File > Language and choose the language you want. The setting applies to that one document, and Google does not list a keyboard shortcut for it, so you use the menu.
tldr: Open the document in Google Docs in your browser, then go to File > Language and pick a language.
The setting covers that one document. Repeat it for each file that needs it.
Google's keyboard shortcuts page lists no shortcut for File > Language.
Want a translated copy instead? Use Tools > Translate document. It makes a new file under the name you enter.
No Translate document item in Tools usually means the file is in Office editing. Convert it to Google Docs first.

blocks.text: Google Docs runs in a browser. I did not find an official Google Docs app for Mac, so these steps assume you open Docs in Chrome or another browser. The menus you need are inside the Docs page, under the document title. They are not the menu bar at the top of your Mac screen. Docs has no version numbers, so one set of steps covers the current Mac version of Docs.
Step by step: change the language for one document

Use this path when you want Docs to treat a file as a different language. Open the file, then follow the steps in the steps section. You do it once per file. The setting stays with that document, so two files in your Drive can use two different languages.
Before you start: check the file and your browser

items: Open the file in Chrome, the browser these steps assume.
Check the file name at the top of the page. Make sure it is the file you mean.
Confirm you have edit access. A view-only file may gray out the File menu.
Keep the Docs tab in front while you work, so the menu you click belongs to the right file.

blocks.text: If the Tools menu has no Translate document item, Google says the file is probably open in Microsoft Office editing. Convert it to Google Docs first, then come back to these steps. Google's help page gives this as the reason the item is missing, so start there if you see that gap.
What File > Language does and does not do

File > Language sets the language for the document you have open. Google's help page describes it as a per-document setting. Other files keep their own language. The setting does not translate the text. Translate document does that, and it makes a copy instead of changing the original.

I could not confirm every option in the Language submenu, or what each choice changes in every feature. The Google help pages I checked do not list those details, so this guide does not promise them. Test the result before you rely on it, as the next sections show.
Why the document language matters

The language setting tells Docs which language the file is written in. That matters when you share a draft with people who read in another language, or when you hand the file to a proofreader. A file with the wrong label can cause confusion for the people who check it. The label takes a few seconds to set, so set it before you share the file, not after.
Test that the change took effect

A menu click is not proof. Click at the end of the text and type a short sentence in the new language. Read it back and check that the line looks the way you expect. Then open File > Language again and confirm the choice is the one you meant.
Delete the test line when you finish. A stray sentence in a shared file is easy to miss, and reviewers will see it before you do.
A quick check after you change the language

items: Read the title and the first paragraph out loud, or in your head, in the new language.
Check that headings and list labels still make sense.
Open File > Language once more and confirm the choice.
Delete any test text you typed.
Only then share the file or send it for review.

blocks.text: Is there a keyboard shortcut for document language?

Not one that Google documents. The keyboard shortcuts page lists Input tools on or off as ⌘⇧K and Select input tools as ⌘⌥⇧K on Mac. It lists no shortcut for spell check or language settings. Some guides online name other shortcuts for this task. Do not rely on them unless Google's own page lists them too.
Input tools are a different feature

People mix up Input tools with the document language, and it is an easy mix-up. Input tools change how you type, which helps when you write in another writing system. They are a separate feature from File > Language. Treat them as two separate settings.
Use ⌘⇧K to turn Input tools on or off. Use ⌘⌥⇧K to select an input tool. The tools on offer depend on what Docs lists, so read the menu on your screen before you choose one.
Translate a document instead of changing its language

Choose Tools > Translate document when you want a second copy in another language. Docs asks for a name for the translated copy. It then asks for a language, and you click Translate. The name prompt tells you the result is a new file, not an edit to the one you have open.

Use this path when a reader needs the text in another language. Use File > Language when you only need Docs to treat the file as that language. Picking the wrong path leaves you with an extra file to clean up.

Example: you write a grant summary in English for a reviewer who reads Spanish. Keep the English file as your master. Run Tools > Translate document, name the copy Summary (Spanish), pick Spanish, and click Translate. You now have two files, and each one needs its own proofread.
Change the language for more than one document

Do the File > Language step on every file that needs it. The setting does not spread across a folder. Open each file, make the change, and close it. Keep a short list in a note so you can tick files off as you go, and so you do not change one twice.

If you make the same kind of file often, a template can save you from repeating the setup each time. Read [How to create a template in Google Docs on Mac: step by step for 2026](/how-to/create-a-template-in-google-docs) before you build one.
Common mistakes when changing document language

items: Changing the wrong open file. Check the file name at the top before you click.
Looking for the setting in the Mac menu bar at the top of the screen. Docs has its own menus inside the page, so the setting lives under File.
Expecting a Mac keyboard shortcut. Google lists none for File > Language.
Using Tools > Translate document when you only wanted the setting. That makes a second file, so you end up with two to manage.
Mixing up Input tools with the document language. Input tools change typing, not the document setting.

blocks.text: Skipping the test is the last common mistake. Read one line after you change the setting. That check is much quicker than fixing a document after people have already read it.
Working offline with a language change

Offline editing in Google Docs needs Google Chrome or Microsoft Edge. You also need the Google Docs Offline extension installed and turned on. Setup needs an internet connection, and private browsing is not supported.

Make the language change while you are online, then turn on offline access. If your admin has blocked offline access, you may see the message 'Offline sync is disabled by your administrator'. Only your admin can change that, so ask them before you plan your work around offline editing.
Where to go next

If you need voice help while you write, read [How to use voice typing in Google Docs on Mac: a step by step guide](/how-to/use-voice-typing-in-google-docs). For offline setup, see [How to turn on offline mode in Google Docs on Mac: step by step in Chrome](/how-to/turn-on-offline-mode-in-google-docs).

Keep these steps in your notes. Menus in web apps can move when the software changes. When a menu name differs on your screen, search the Docs menus for Language first, then look for the same words in the File menu.

faq.question: Can I change the language for all my Google Docs at once?
faq.answer: Not with the File menu. The setting is per document, so you change each file on its own. The Google help pages I checked do not cover changing a default language for your whole account, so this guide gives no steps for that.

faq.question: Where is File > Language in Google Docs on Mac?
faq.answer: Open the document, then click File in the Docs menu bar under the title. Move to Language to open its submenu. It sits inside the Docs page, not in the menu bar at the top of your Mac screen.

faq.question: Is there a keyboard shortcut to change document language on Mac?
faq.answer: Google's keyboard shortcuts page lists none for File > Language. It does list Input tools shortcuts, ⌘⇧K and ⌘⌥⇧K, but those control typing tools, not the document setting.

faq.question: What is the difference between File > Language and Translate document?
faq.answer: File > Language sets the language of the file you have open. Tools > Translate document creates a new translated copy, and you name that copy before you click Translate.

faq.question: Does Google Docs work offline on a Mac?
faq.answer: Yes, with conditions. You need Google Chrome or Microsoft Edge, the Google Docs Offline extension turned on, and an internet connection to set it up. Private browsing is not supported.

faq.question: Do these steps work in Safari?
faq.answer: I did not check Safari for this setting, so I cannot confirm it behaves the same there. Google's offline help names Chrome and Edge. Use Chrome if you want these steps to match exactly.

task: Change a Google Docs document language on Mac
appliesTo: Google Docs in a browser on macOS, for any document you can edit
requirements: A Google Docs file open in Chrome or another browser
Edit access to the file, since view-only access can gray out menus
Chrome or Edge only if you want offline editing

steps.name: Open the document in Google Docs
steps.text: Open the file in your browser. Check the file name at the top of the page. Make sure it is a Google Docs file, not a Word file open in Office editing.
steps.tip: No Translate document item under Tools usually means the file is in Office editing. Convert it to Google Docs first.

steps.name: Open the File menu
steps.text: Click File in the Docs menu bar, just under the document title. This is the menu inside the Docs page, not the menu bar at the top of your Mac screen.
steps.tip: If File is grayed out or missing items, you may have view-only access. Ask the owner for edit access.

steps.name: Open the Language submenu
steps.text: Move the pointer over Language in the File menu. The submenu opens to the side. Click Language if the submenu does not open on its own.
steps.tip: Google's help page names this path. It does not list every submenu option, so read the list on your screen.

steps.name: Pick the language you want
steps.text: Click the language you want from the list. The change applies to this open document only. Other files keep the language they had before.
steps.tip: Choose one language per document. If you are unsure, ask the person who will read the file.

steps.name: Test the new setting
steps.text: Click at the end of the text. Type a short sentence and read it back. Then open File > Language again and confirm the choice is the one you meant.
steps.tip: Delete the test sentence when you finish, so it does not end up in the final file.

steps.name: Repeat for each document
steps.text: Open the next file and repeat steps 2 to 4. Keep a short list of the files you have finished, so you do not skip one.
steps.tip: The setting is per document. A file you skip keeps its old language.

troubleshooting.problem: Translate document is missing from the Tools menu
troubleshooting.fix: Google says the file is probably open in Microsoft Office editing. Convert it to Google Docs first, then check the Tools menu again.

troubleshooting.problem: The language change applies to one file only
troubleshooting.fix: That is how the setting works. Google's help page describes it per document. Repeat File > Language in every file that needs it.

troubleshooting.problem: I cannot find the File menu
troubleshooting.fix: Make sure the Google Docs page is open in a browser. Look inside the page, under the title, for File. The Mac menu bar at the top of the screen does not show it.

troubleshooting.problem: A Mac shortcut from another guide does nothing
troubleshooting.fix: Google's keyboard shortcuts page lists none for File > Language. Use the menu. The Input tools shortcuts control typing, not the document language.

troubleshooting.problem: Offline editing says the document could not sync
troubleshooting.fix: Check your network connection. Then turn Make available offline off and on from the File menu, as Google's offline help page describes.

troubleshooting.problem: Offline sync is disabled by your administrator
troubleshooting.fix: Your admin has blocked offline access for this account. Ask them to allow it, or keep working online.
